slides.body: This course teaches California rules of the road: signs, signals, right-of-way, speed, and sharing the road. Move through each lesson in order.
slides.say: This course teaches California rules of the road: signs, signals, right-of-way, speed, and sharing the road. Move through each lesson in order.

slides.title: California learner's permit
slides.body: To get a provisional instruction permit in California you typically need to pass a vision exam and a knowledge test, complete required application steps, and meet age/education requirements. Confirm current rules on dmv.ca.gov before you apply.
slides.say: To get a provisional instruction permit in California you typically need to pass a vision exam and a knowledge test, complete required application steps, and meet age/education requirements. Confirm current rules on dmv.ca.gov before you apply.
slides.activity: Name two steps you need before a provisional permit.
examples: You are 16, finish the application steps, pass vision and knowledge tests.
You confirm age and education rules on dmv.ca.gov before you go.
You bring required ID documents — not just a phone screenshot of grades.
slides.quiz_prompt: What do you typically need for a California provisional instruction permit?
quiz_choices: Vision exam, knowledge test, and required application steps
Only a written note from a parent
A full driver’s license from another country
Proof you already own a car
slides.quiz_explanation: Confirm current DMV rules — they can change.
slides.game_prompt: Order the usual permit path
game_options: Vision exam, knowledge test, and required application steps

slides.title: Right-of-way at stops
slides.body: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to arrive goes first. If two arrive together, yield to the driver on your right. Yield to pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks and to emergency vehicles with lights and sirens.
slides.say: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to arrive goes first. If two arrive together, yield to the driver on your right. Yield to pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks and to emergency vehicles with lights and sirens.
slides.activity: At a four-way stop, who goes first if you arrive together?
examples: You arrive first at a four-way stop — you go when clear.
You and another car arrive together — you yield to the driver on your right.
An ambulance approaches with lights and sirens — everyone yields.
slides.quiz_prompt: At a four-way stop, if two cars arrive together, who goes first?
quiz_choices: The driver on the right
Whoever honks first
The larger vehicle
The driver turning left always
slides.quiz_explanation: First to arrive goes first; if tied, yield to the right. Always yield to pedestrians and emergency vehicles.
slides.game_prompt: At a four-way stop, if two cars arrive together, who goes first?
game_options: The driver on the right

The larger vehicle

slides.title: California speed basics
slides.body: California’s Basic Speed Law: never drive faster than is safe for conditions, even below the posted limit. Common posted limits include 25 mph in business or residential districts unless posted otherwise, and higher freeway limits as posted.
slides.say: California’s Basic Speed Law: never drive faster than is safe for conditions, even below the posted limit. Common posted limits include 25 mph in business or residential districts unless posted otherwise, and higher freeway limits as posted.
slides.activity: Say the Basic Speed Law in one sentence.
examples: Rain is heavy — you drive below the posted limit because conditions demand it.
A residential street is posted 25 mph unless another limit is posted.
A clear freeway shows a higher posted limit — you still obey Basic Speed Law.
slides.quiz_prompt: California’s Basic Speed Law means:
quiz_choices: Never drive faster than is safe for conditions, even below the posted limit
You may exceed the limit if no police are visible
Posted limits do not apply in rain
Only freeways have speed rules
slides.quiz_explanation: Safe for conditions always beats “the number on the sign.”
slides.game_prompt: California’s Basic Speed Law means:
game_options: Never drive faster than is safe for conditions, even below the posted limit
You may exceed the limit if no police are visible
Posted limits do not apply in rain

slides.title: Following distance
slides.body: Use at least a three-second following gap in good conditions. Increase space in rain, fog, night, heavy traffic, or when following large trucks and motorcycles.
slides.say: Use at least a three-second following gap in good conditions. Increase space in rain, fog, night, heavy traffic, or when following large trucks and motorcycles.
slides.activity: Count a three-second gap out loud.
examples: In dry daylight you pick a fixed landmark and count three seconds behind a car.
Fog rolls in — you increase the gap beyond three seconds.
You follow a motorcycle — you leave extra space.
slides.quiz_prompt: In good conditions, what following gap should you aim for?
quiz_choices: At least three seconds
One car length only
Half a second if you are late
Whatever the car behind you uses
slides.quiz_explanation: Increase space in rain, fog, night, traffic, or near large trucks.
slides.game_prompt: In good conditions, what following gap should you aim for?
game_options: At least three seconds
One car length only
Half a second if you are late

slides.title: Signals and lane changes
slides.body: Signal before turns and lane changes. Check mirrors, signal, check your blind spot over your shoulder, then move smoothly. Do not change lanes in an intersection.
slides.say: Signal before turns and lane changes. Check mirrors, signal, check your blind spot over your shoulder, then move smoothly. Do not change lanes in an intersection.
slides.activity: List the mirror–signal–blind-spot order.
examples: Before changing lanes: mirrors, signal, shoulder check, then move smoothly.
You decide not to change lanes inside an intersection.
You signal early so others can predict your turn.
slides.quiz_prompt: Correct lane-change order is closest to:
quiz_choices: Check mirrors, signal, check blind spot, then move
Move first, then signal if someone honks
Signal only after you are in the new lane

slides.quiz_explanation: Never change lanes in an intersection.
slides.game_prompt: Order a safe lane change
game_options: Check mirrors, signal, check blind spot, then move

slides.title: Turning and red lights
slides.body: California generally allows a right turn on red after a complete stop unless a sign prohibits it. Yield to pedestrians and cross traffic. Left on red is only allowed from a one-way street onto a one-way street when permitted.
slides.say: California generally allows a right turn on red after a complete stop unless a sign prohibits it. Yield to pedestrians and cross traffic. Left on red is only allowed from a one-way street onto a one-way street when permitted.
slides.activity: When is a right turn on red allowed in California?
examples: Right on red after a full stop is usually OK unless a sign bans it — you still yield.
You stop completely behind the line before turning right on red.
Left on red is only from one-way onto one-way when allowed — you verify.
slides.quiz_prompt: In California, a right turn on red generally requires:
quiz_choices: A complete stop, then yield to pedestrians and cross traffic (unless prohibited)
Rolling through if the way looks empty
Honking instead of stopping
Turning only after the light turns green
slides.quiz_explanation: Signs can prohibit right on red — always look.

game_options: A complete stop, then yield to pedestrians and cross traffic (unless prohibited)

Honking instead of stopping

slides.title: School buses in California
slides.body: When a school bus displays flashing red lights and a stop signal arm on an undivided roadway, traffic in both directions must stop. On a divided highway, only traffic traveling the same direction as the bus must stop. Stay stopped until the lights stop and the arm is withdrawn.
slides.say: When a school bus displays flashing red lights and a stop signal arm on an undivided roadway, traffic in both directions must stop. On a divided highway, only traffic traveling the same direction as the bus must stop. Stay stopped until the lights stop and the arm is withdrawn.
slides.activity: Who must stop for flashing red bus lights on an undivided road?
examples: Undivided road, bus has red lights + stop arm — traffic both ways stops.
Divided highway — only same-direction traffic must stop.
Lights stop and arm withdraws — you proceed when safe.
slides.quiz_prompt: On an undivided roadway, who must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and stop arm?
quiz_choices: Traffic in both directions
Only cars behind the bus
Only cars coming from the left

slides.quiz_explanation: On divided highways, only same-direction traffic must stop.
slides.game_prompt: On an undivided roadway, who must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and stop arm?
game_options: Traffic in both directions

slides.title: Seat belts and phones
slides.body: California requires seat belt use. Handheld phone use while driving is restricted — use hands-free or pull over safely. Distracted driving citations and crash risk are high; put the phone away.
slides.say: California requires seat belt use. Handheld phone use while driving is restricted — use hands-free or pull over safely. Distracted driving citations and crash risk are high; put the phone away.

You need to text — you pull over safely instead of holding the phone.

quiz_choices: Restricted — use hands-free or pull over safely
Allowed anytime under 25 mph
Required for navigation screens

slides.title: DUI limits (California)
slides.body: For drivers 21+, the BAC limit is 0.08%. Drivers under 21 are subject to zero-tolerance rules. Commercial drivers have a lower limit. Never drive impaired — arrange another ride.
slides.say: For drivers 21+, the BAC limit is 0.08%. Drivers under 21 are subject to zero-tolerance rules. Commercial drivers have a lower limit. Never drive impaired — arrange another ride.

quiz_choices: 0.00% for all ages with no exceptions listed elsewhere
slides.quiz_explanation: Under 21: zero tolerance. Never drive impaired.

game_options: 0.00% for all ages with no exceptions listed elsewhere

slides.title: What to do after a crash
slides.body: If safe, move out of traffic and turn on hazards. Call 911 for injuries. Exchange names, contact, license, and insurance info. Do not argue fault at the scene; report as required.
slides.say: If safe, move out of traffic and turn on hazards. Call 911 for injuries. Exchange names, contact, license, and insurance info. Do not argue fault at the scene; report as required.

Someone is hurt — you call 911.
You exchange license, contact, and insurance info without arguing fault.

quiz_choices: Move out of traffic if safe, hazards on, help injured, exchange info
Leave immediately to avoid paperwork

slides.quiz_explanation: Do not argue fault at the scene; report as required.

game_options: Move out of traffic if safe, hazards on, help injured, exchange info

slides.body: White rectangular signs with black or red markings tell you what you must or must not do: speed limits, Do Not Enter, One Way, and No U-Turn. A red octagon is always STOP.

slides.title: Yield and stop
slides.body: A red-and-white triangle is YIELD — slow and give way. A stop sign requires a complete stop behind the limit line or crosswalk before proceeding when clear.
slides.say: A red-and-white triangle is YIELD — slow and give way. A stop sign requires a complete stop behind the limit line or crosswalk before proceeding when clear.
slides.activity: Difference between yield and a full stop?

Stop sign: full stop behind the limit line or crosswalk.

slides.quiz_prompt: A red-and-white triangle sign means:
quiz_choices: YIELD — slow and give way
STOP completely always

slides.quiz_explanation: Stop requires a complete stop; yield means give way.

slides.title: Warning signs
slides.body: Yellow diamond signs warn of curves, merges, pedestrians, school zones, and slippery roads. Slow and prepare to react; they do not always require a full stop.

slides.body: Green signs guide routes and exits. Blue signs mark services (fuel, food, lodging). Brown signs mark parks and recreation.

slides.title: Traffic signals
slides.body: Green means go if clear; yellow means prepare to stop if safe; red means stop. Flashing red = stop sign. Flashing yellow = proceed with caution.
slides.say: Green means go if clear; yellow means prepare to stop if safe; red means stop. Flashing red = stop sign. Flashing yellow = proceed with caution.

Flashing yellow = proceed with caution.
Steady red = stop; green = go if clear.

quiz_choices: Stop — same idea as a stop sign

Yield only to trucks

slides.body: Yellow lines separate opposite directions; white lines separate same-direction lanes. A solid line on your side means do not pass or change lanes across it.

slides.title: Railroad crossings
slides.body: Never cross when lights flash or gates lower. Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. If stalled on tracks, exit immediately and move away at an angle toward the oncoming train.
slides.say: Never cross when lights flash or gates lower. Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. If stalled on tracks, exit immediately and move away at an angle toward the oncoming train.

slides.title: Roundabouts
slides.body: Yield to traffic already in the circle, enter when clear, and signal when exiting. Do not stop inside the circulating roadway.
slides.say: Yield to traffic already in the circle, enter when clear, and signal when exiting. Do not stop inside the circulating roadway.
